newsitem.title: UK: Asia draws upwards of 1.8 mln tonnes Europe gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Asia draws upwards of 1.8 mln tonnes Europe gas oil.

text.p: Heavy Asian demand has drawn between 1.5 to 1.8 million tonnes of European gas oil since the beginning of March and more could still go, traders said on Tuesday.
"The arb is still open at around $3-4 a tonne, even with the high freight rates, so there is still interest for fob cargoes," said one trader.
Strong interest in Singapore and to a lesser degree in India has been supporting the European market by drawing away barrels for the last month or so from a fairly disinterested local market.
"There are no more fob barrels available out of Italy, there have all been set for Asia," said one Mediterranean trader.
In the north, Russian gas oil, which has formed the bulk of the cargoes heading eastwards, is tight for large 55,000 tonnes and above - the cargoes that are "arbitrage friendly".
But not all market players are relaxed about how long Asian demand will last and some have become cautious about shifting material past April 15-20.
One senior shipbroker in London said it looked like the arb was shutting because the last couple of ships that were supposed to be heading to Asia from Europe had failed their fixtures.
But one gas oil trader thought the failed fixings could mean that the charterer had been unable to secure enough product to fill the ship.
Should Asian prices decline and shut the arbitrage window the prospect for European gas oil will be gloomy, traders said.
"If the arb closes the Med will collapse," said one citing only moderate European interest for gas oil given the continent's mild winter.
The situation could be further complicated by the increasing tightness of tonnage.

Shipping brokers said tanker owners with vessels heading to Asia will have to start making a decision on whether to ballast back to Europe or whether to spend time in the region doing local Asian trips.
"If there aren't enough ships to take the material to Asia the arb just becomes notional," said one trader.
Singapore buying for heating oil and diesel continued apace with a record 1.9 million barrels of diesel for end April/early May lifting exchanging hands last week.

The volume of trade has seriously thinned spot storage space in Singapore and storage prices have more than doubled to between 40-50 cents a barrel compared with 15 cents about one month ago, Singapore traders said.
Singapore has the largest independent storage facility in the Asia-Pacific region with more than 3.5 million cubic metres of capacity.
